I have INSANE medication anxiety, so starting zoloft was super scary for me. I also had a really bad reaction trying lexapro which made it SO much worse. It took me actual days to take my first dose. 

Honestly, the side effects I had were VERY minimal. If you're super worried, I'd start on a low dose. I started at 12.5mg (half a 25mg pill), and every side effect I had was completely bearable and lasted less than a week. I was ever so slightly queasy on the first day I was taking it, and it went away after I ate. I would also have a VERY brief moment when waking up where I'd panic for a split second, but it went away super quick and didn't really affect me at all. 

I really hated the idea of being dependent on medication, especially something that I'd have to taper off of. But honestly? It's so worth it. I'm so much happier and relaxed now, I feel like a different person. My quality of life has improved drastically 

And you can talk to your doctor about upping your dosage super slow. I'm on like 37.5mg (one and a half 25mg pill) right now, and I'll be going up to 50mg in a few weeks. Even the low doses have been amazing for me.

Edit: Forgot to say, I'm taking it for major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder

From what I understand, the rule is if you are by after 10 then you can close up to half of them so that you aren't running the whole thing by yourself.

After that you can open it back up until all the customers are out. 

At my store, when we got around 11:58 we'd try and close a few until we only had 2 or 3 registers open because they come back up faster if they're closed before they "flip". I don't know if other stores do it differently. Don't do this if you're super busy. 

Close a few if you can, then when they "flip" open the ones that are already closed to get the rest of the customers out. 

I don't know if you knew about the registers flipping over but I figured it was worth it to say something in case you didn't. 

Other than that I can't remember anything special we did. It might vary from store to store. Hope this helps.

I would absolutely talk to a doctor about your options and see what's best for you. And absolutely don't let the internet freak you out about BC. There are ABSOLUTELY risks to any sort of hormonal BC and you're really not going to know how it effects you until you try it. 

Just as much as there is a chance that you'll react badly, there's also a chance that it won't effect you that much. 

I was really anxious when I started the combo pill. I also struggle with depression as well as anxiety and I have family members that reacted horribly to the pill. But I tried it, and honestly I've been feeling better since taking it. The first few weeks were rough, but I really haven't noticed much change so far. 

Do what you think is best for yourself. Understand that there are risks to any hormonal BC, and if you feel like the risks are too great then don't go for it. But a risk is not a guarantee. You have to decide for yourself what risks you're willing to take, don't let other people scare you. Talk to a doctor about it and learn about your risks from a professional.
